evidence: src/domain/task-status.ts defines `taskStatuses`, `TaskStatus` and `isTaskStatus` once; src/domain/task.ts (`status: TaskStatus`) and src/domain/repositories.ts (`TaskFilter.status?: TaskStatus`) both use this type and do not redefine the status values
src/domain/project.ts, src/domain/user.ts and src/domain/task.ts all throw `DomainError` from src/domain/errors.ts when an invariant is broken, so errors are reported the same way across the module
src/domain/task.ts `markDone()` returns a new Task through the constructor, so the constructor's validation is reused rather than repeated
src/domain/repositories.ts declares `ProjectRepository`, `UserRepository` and `TaskRepository`, typed only against the module's entities Project, User and Task
src/domain/project.ts and src/domain/user.ts each check `!id.trim() || !name.trim()` for their own entity. These are separate entity invariants, not one rule that should be centralized
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All six files belong to one concern: the task-management domain model. That covers the entities (Project, User, Task), the TaskStatus value set, the DomainError type and the repository ports. Each file uses the module's own abstractions the same way. Every entity reports a broken invariant by throwing DomainError. Task and TaskFilter both use the TaskStatus type, which is defined once in task-status.ts. The repository interfaces are typed only against the module's own entities. Each invariant lives in one place. The list of statuses and its guard live only in task-status.ts. The due-date and title rules live only in Task's constructor. The rule that a task cannot be marked done twice lives only in Task.markDone. Project and User each check that their own id and name are not blank. These are separate invariants on separate entities, not one shared rule copied in two places, so this does not count as harmful duplication. No file goes around the module's abstractions, and no file has a concern unrelated to the rest.
